recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-15909 unless the Security work group separately chooses to revise the already-present input-validation guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-15909 was a Published/Persuasive Security work group change request from the STU3 cycle asking to add an Input Validation item to the top summary list on the FHIR Security page. The requested wording said to validate all input received from other actors so the data is well formed and does not contain content that would cause unwanted system behavior, with testing examples such as fuzzing, invalid input attacks, and injection attacks; Jira comments cautioned that the testing examples should not be read as exhaustive or prescriptive.
initial_application: Git commit 95ee245e72e4bd1ac09824738ae7b5f7519239ef, titled 'Approved security narrative fixes. GF#15907, GF#15909, ...', added the Input Validation bullet to source/security.html. Current source retains that recommendation.
additional_context: source/hierarchy.xml lists source/security.html as the Security page under the active Security and Privacy module, confirming build scope. Later commits 60e98c41f6c5fab597bbdb8d7ec41898ca4ec777 and 9fc7e6315ee8cec47164c29c1814ca69660e40a8 changed spelling and removed broken anchors while preserving the FHIR-15909 substance. Jira, Zulip, and Confluence searches found no later substantive decision that contradicts the current wording.
reconciliation: No source edit was made because source/security.html already includes the Input Validation summary item and the requested testing examples. The published combined-branch commit is an empty audit commit documenting that no change is needed.
